question: With value K fixed at 32, which fixed causal spatial predecessor count minimizes the paid physical archive over the same 50 exposed HEST development slices?
data_role: exposed development calibration; not independent confirmation
warmup_rule: Rows with fewer than M predecessors use the gene base probability; conditional odds are used once M predecessors are available.
graph_rule: For row i, select up to M prior rows j<i by squared Euclidean distance; ties use ascending prior row index. Source row order is preserved.
graph_accounting: The production six-neighbor graph is retained for the fixed value branch. Spatial M<=6 reuses its first M columns at zero incremental graph cost; spatial M>6 stores and pays only columns 6:M. ROW_M06 is regenerated from row index and M without a stored graph.
primary_endpoint: pooled full physical archive bytes for each fixed spatial M
selection_rule: Compute 100*(candidate_bytes-minimum_bytes)/minimum_bytes for spatial arms; values <=0.05 percent are tied and the smaller M is selected. Leave-largest-saver-out removes the most negative per-slice byte delta versus M6 before re-summing.
secondary_endpoints: median, Q1 and Q3 of per-slice percent change; quartiles use linear interpolation at sorted index (n-1)*p
support stream, support model, graph and total archive decomposition
failure_rule: Retain every attempt. One fresh-process retry is allowed only for a native access violation or Numba import/cache failure. Integrity, resource, exactness or second failures stop the run without replacing a sample.
claim_boundary: The selected M is a development-panel fixed default within the tested candidate set, not a universal optimum or independent biological validation.
